question:
A triangular park has vertices $P(-2,4)$, $Q(3,-1)$, and $R(5,5)$.

(a) Calculate its area using a determinant.

(b) A point $S(t,2)$ is chosen so that the area of $\triangle PQS$ is half the area of $\triangle PQR$. Determine all possible values of $t$.

(c) Verify the area of $\triangle PQS$ for each value of $t$.
explanation:
(a)
$$\text{Area of }\triangle PQR=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}-2 & 4 & 1\\3 & -1 & 1\\5 & 5 & 1\end{vmatrix}\right|$$
Expanding the determinant,
$$\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}|(-2)(-6)-4(3-5)+(15+5)|$$
$$\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}|12+8+20|=20$$
Therefore, the area of $\triangle PQR$ is $20$ square units.

(b)
The required area of $\triangle PQS$ is
$$\frac{1}{2}(20)=10$$
Now,
$$\text{Area of }\triangle PQS=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}-2 & 4 & 1\\3 & -1 & 1\\t & 2 & 1\end{vmatrix}\right|$$
$$=\frac{1}{2}|(-2)(-3)-4(3-t)+(6+t)|$$
$$=\frac{1}{2}|6-12+4t+6+t|=\frac{1}{2}|5t|$$
Therefore,
$$\frac{5}{2}|t|=10$$
$$|t|=4$$
Hence,
$$t=4\quad\text{or}\quad t=-4$$

(c)
For $t=4$,
$$\text{Area of }\triangle PQS=\frac{1}{2}|5(4)|=10$$
For $t=-4$,
$$\text{Area of }\triangle PQS=\frac{1}{2}|5(-4)|=10$$
Thus, both values give the required area of $10$ square units.

options.A:
(a) Area of $\triangle PQR=20$ square units
(b) $t=4$ only
(c) Area of $\triangle PQS=10$ square units
options.B:
(a) Area of $\triangle PQR=20$ square units
(b) $t=4$ or $t=-4$
(c) For both values, area of $\triangle PQS=10$ square units
options.C:
(a) Area of $\triangle PQR=40$ square units
(b) $t=4$ or $t=-4$
(c) For both values, area of $\triangle PQS=20$ square units
options.D:
(a) Area of $\triangle PQR=20$ square units
(b) $t=2$ or $t=-2$
(c) For both values, area of $\triangle PQS=5$ square units
